## The finding

`crime_00011` — **Timezone Roulette** (`timezone_unsafe_parse`), `src/date.ts:29,33`, confidence 0.9:

> 2 `new Date("…")` calls parsing a string with no timezone marker.
> unsafe literals: `"2026-12-25T07:00:00"`, `"2026-12-20"`

Both are flagged, but they are **not** parsed by the same rule, and that distinction is the whole bug:

| Literal | Line | Function | ES spec parse rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"2026-12-20"` | 33 | `startOfPromoWindow()` | date-only → **UTC** midnight |
| `"2026-12-25T07:00:00"` | 29 | `christmasMorning()` | date-*time*, no zone → **host local** |

## The literal responsible

The promo window is owned by **`"2026-12-20"` at `src/date.ts:33`** (`startOfPromoWindow`).

One thing I want to state plainly rather than paper over: as written, that literal is *not* what produces "a day early in Europe." Date-only strings parse as UTC midnight on every conforming engine, so `startOfPromoWindow()` returns the identical instant on a UTC CI box and a CET production box. If anything it opens an hour **late** for a CET user (01:00 local on the 20th).

The direction described in the report — earlier in absolute time as the UTC offset goes positive — is the signature of the **local-parse** rule, the one governing line 29. A boundary written as `"2026-12-20T00:00:00"` (no `Z`) is `2026-12-19T23:00:00Z` in CET: a day early, in Europe, passing in UTC CI. That is the exact failure the ticket describes. So either the promo gate is reading the line 29 literal, or `startOfPromoWindow` has been edited to the zone-less datetime form since this scan. Worth confirming against the actual gate before you sign off on a cause.

Either way, the fix below is the same and covers both.

## Smallest change

Pin both literals to an explicit zone. No signature change, no rename, no library:

```ts
export function christmasMorning(): Date {
  return new Date("2026-12-25T07:00:00Z");   // + Z
}

export function startOfPromoWindow(): Date {
  return new Date("2026-12-20T00:00:00Z");   // spell out the UTC that was already implied
}
```

Line 29 is a one-character edit and is a genuine behaviour change: it removes the host-timezone dependency, which is what makes prod match CI. Line 33 is behaviour-preserving — it makes the existing UTC semantics visible so the next editor doesn't "helpfully" expand it into the zone-less datetime form and reintroduce the bug.

If the promo is meant to open at midnight *Brussels time*, `Z` is the wrong constant and you want `"2026-12-20T00:00:00+01:00"` — but that's a product decision, not a bug fix, and it will make the CI test fail correctly.

## One thing this fix does not close

`crime_00009` — **Half-UTC, Half-Local** (`src/date.ts:9,41`, severity high) — is the other half of the same class of bug. `dateLabel()` at line 41 reads `getUTCFullYear()` alongside `getMonth()`/`getDate()`, so it will still render a date whose year comes from one time domain and whose month/day come from another. Pinning the parse fixes the *boundary*; it does not fix the *rendering*. If the "opens a day early" report came from what a user saw on screen rather than from when the gate flipped, line 41 is your actual culprit and this fix won't move it.
